title: Wyoming Valley West School Board addresses ongoing social media post investigation - NewsBreak
text:
By Sydney Allabaugh [email protected] ,
1 hours ago Dwayne McDavitt, a Larksville resident, addresses the board. Sydney Allabaugh | Times Leader Wyoming Valley West School Board addressed the ongoing investigation into a social media post regarding the killing of right-wing activist Charlie Kirk made from the “compromised” account of a school administrator after its reorganization meeting on Wednesday.
Dwayne McDavitt, a Larksville resident, addressed the board at the work session that followed the reorganization meeting at 7 p.m. at the middle school in Kingston.
“When a staff member publicly posts celebratory or negative comments about someone’s death, regardless of who it is, it can raise questions about the judgment, emotional maturity, and ability to model appropriate behavior for the students,” McDavitt told the board.
He asked if they had come to a decision about how to proceed with the investigation and asked for updates regarding a right-to-know request for close to 5,000 emails on which the administrator was included.
The board replied that it was a topic of discussion in the executive session and that they are weighing their options to find a timely and inexpensive solution. They are looking to find a company to review the files so they can turn over what they are legally required to.
“You have freedom of speech, but when you work for the public, you have a code of ethics, a code of conduct, and a social media policy you have to go by,” McDavitt said.
The district’s social media policy is publicly accessible under the policies tab on the school website.
The policy states that the district respects employees’ free speech and does not actively monitor social media accounts. However, it says, “Speech that takes place off-site and on an employee’s own time, including posting on personal social media accounts, may be addressed if the district establishes that the employee’s expression infringed on the interests of the district in promoting the efficient and effective functioning and educational purpose of the district.”
It also states, “When an employee speaks as a citizen on a matter of public concern, the district shall consult with the school solicitor in determining the appropriate course of action, in accordance with applicable law, regulations, and board policy.”
Other business
At the reorganization meeting preceding the work session, new members Joshua Bellio and Jack Nicholson, along with incumbents Janet Cussatt and John Perfetto, who all ran unopposed in the Nov. 6 election, were sworn in.
They will replace William Hardwick and former vice president Paul Keating, who did not seek reelection. Nicholas Wilson was named vice president of the board. Charles Kamus will remain president.
New member Bellio said he was hesitant to run but wanted to play an active role in improving the school after having put his children through it.
“If I could do anything different or good for the community, why not?” Bellio said.
Bellio, as the owner of Bellio Plumbing and Heating, said he hopes to create improvements to the technical school.
Nicholson also mentioned his objectives.
“I feel education, safety, and security for the Wyoming Valley West School District are the key goals here,” he said.
The school board will hold its next regular meeting at 7 p.m. on Dec. 10 at the middle school.
Meetings are open to the public and can be accessed via Zoom.
